page.title: AI Models
page.subtitle: Explore the neural networks developed for defect detection in PCBs.

intro.title: Problem Overview
intro.description: Defect detection on Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) is highly challenging in the manufacturing industry: microscopic defects occupy less than 1% of the image (extreme class imbalance), vary widely in scale, and require decisions in milliseconds for real-time assembly lines. We developed and evaluated 4 different Computer Vision architectures to cover all these industrial needs with maximum robustness.

metrics.title: Performance Comparison
metrics.subtitle: Results obtained on the consolidated test set.

conclusions.title: Practical Industrial Conclusions
conclusions.yolo: YOLO11 achieved the highest macro precision (0.9635) and macro F1 (0.9734) among the four evaluated models.
conclusions.fasterrcnn: Faster R-CNN achieved the highest mAP@50 (0.9864) and macro recall (99.24%), with macro precision of 0.8303.
conclusions.retinanet: RetinaNet achieved mAP@50 of 0.8690 and macro precision of 0.5632. False positives indicate a need for adjustments before inspection use.
conclusions.rtdetr: RT-DETR achieved mAP@50 of 0.9845 and macro F1 of 0.9381. These detection results do not measure inference speed.

yolo.howItWorks: YOLO11 processes the entire image in a single neural network pass (Single-stage). It predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly without using pre-defined anchors, reducing computing complexity.
yolo.pcbContext: The main benefit in production is its incredible processing speed (high FPS). With the PANet Neck, it fuses features across scales, preventing tiny defects from slipping through on the conveyor belt.
yolo.expectative: The latest evaluation achieved mAP@50 of 0.9845, macro F1 of 0.9734, macro precision of 0.9635 and macro recall of 0.9838.
yolo.name: YOLO11

fasterrcnn.howItWorks: Uses a dedicated module called RPN (Region Proposal Network) to first propose potential regions likely to contain defects (Stage 1). Then, a deep classifier meticulously inspects these proposals to frame the final defect (Stage 2).
fasterrcnn.pcbContext: Acts essentially like a digital magnifying glass on the board. By adopting the deep ResNet-50-FPN V2 backbone instead of lighter networks, the ability to find microscopic track breaks or missing holes jumped drastically.
fasterrcnn.expectative: The latest evaluation achieved mAP@50 of 0.9864, macro F1 of 0.9034, macro precision of 0.8303 and macro recall of 0.9924.
fasterrcnn.name: Faster R-CNN

retinanet.howItWorks: Although a fast single-stage detector, it implements the Focal Loss function. This math penalizes network errors heavily on hard defect classes and downweights the loss generated by normal board regions (background).
retinanet.pcbContext: On a PCB where 99% of the image represents defect-free background, standard anchors would generate continuous false positives. Focal Loss forces the network's attention purely onto track anomalies and missing holes.
retinanet.expectative: The latest evaluation achieved mAP@50 of 0.8690, macro F1 of 0.6902, macro precision of 0.5632 and macro recall of 0.9319.
retinanet.name: RetinaNet

rtdetr.howItWorks: Uses CNNs only for initial feature extraction and passes them to a Transformer Encoder-Decoder. Self-Attention mechanisms analyze the entire board context at once, predicting boxes directly and eliminating NMS post-processing.
rtdetr.pcbContext: Defects like open circuits have visual cues spread across the tracks. Global attention connects these distant regions. Also, the absence of NMS ensures inference time remains constant regardless of how many defects are on the board.
rtdetr.expectative: The latest evaluation achieved mAP@50 of 0.9845, macro F1 of 0.9381, macro precision of 0.8946 and macro recall of 0.9877.
rtdetr.name: RT-DETR

glossary.title: Technical Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Understand the metrics and concepts used in the evaluation of AI models.

map.title: mAP@50 (Mean Average Precision)
map.desc: Global accuracy metric of the detector. Measures how well the model localizes and classifies the defect simultaneously (with at least 50% overlap with the ground truth). The closer to 1.0000 (100%), the better.

f1.title: Macro F1-Score
f1.desc: Arithmetic mean of the F1 scores calculated separately for each class. Each F1 combines precision and recall using their harmonic mean.

precision.title: Precision
precision.desc: Out of all defects pointed out by the model, how many were actually defects. High precision means very few false alarms (avoiding unnecessary rejection of good boards).

recall.title: Recall (Sensitivity)
recall.desc: Out of all actual defects present on the board, how many the model succeeded in detecting. High recall guarantees that almost no defect slips through the inspection (preventing defect escapes to the customer).

singlestage.title: Single-stage
singlestage.desc: Models that detect defect location and class in a single pass through the convolutional network (e.g., YOLO11 and RetinaNet). They are extremely fast, ideal for high-speed conveyor belts.

twostage.title: Two-stage
twostage.desc: Models that perform the task in two separate steps (e.g., Faster R-CNN): first propose candidate regions (magnifying glass) and then classify them in detail. Slower, but surgical for microscopic defects.

anchorfree.title: Anchor-free
anchorfree.desc: Modern approach predicting bounding boxes directly from pixel features without relying on predefined template sizes (anchors). Simplifies architecture, improving speed and detection of out-of-pattern objects.

anchorbased.title: Anchor-based
anchorbased.desc: Traditional approach using pre-calculated bounding box templates of various scales and aspect ratios. The model adjusts these templates to match the actual defects found.

transformers.title: Vision Transformers (ViT)
transformers.desc: Architectures based on global attention mechanisms (e.g., RT-DETR). They analyze the entire image simultaneously, connecting visual clues across distant areas of the board, which helps find complex trace breaks.

focalloss.title: Focal Loss
focalloss.desc: Special loss function designed to handle extreme class imbalance (where 99% of the image is normal board background). It forces the network to ignore easy areas and focus purely on rare and hard-to-detect defect instances.

nms.title: NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression)
nms.desc: Post-processing algorithm that removes overlapping and redundant bounding boxes for the same defect, keeping only the box with the highest confidence score.
